cells.tense: Right now, pen in hand, a plain read of someone close to you is arriving and you are letting it land.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: With someone you know well, take your first clean read of what's going on with them one step further than feels easy, then stop, without acting on it.
cells.core:
A first, plain read of another person is arriving in you. You can tell something is true about them — what they need, what they are avoiding — and you are letting it sit rather than turning it into advice or a correction. That restraint is the whole strength here: you understand them before you decide what to do about them, and connection stays clean because nothing has been forced onto it.
The stretch is to keep going one step past where it feels comfortable. Stay with your first honest read of that person a little longer than you usually would, then stop. Say nothing, change nothing, just let it be accurate for a minute. What you do after that will come from what you saw, not from the need to be done with it.
cells.sheetLine: Let the clear read land before you do anything with it.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before there is anything yet to see
cells.place: where two people are trying to understand each other without distortion

cells.tense: Bracing ahead, you have already built the full picture of someone's inner world before they have shown it to you.
cells.act: carry what the spark became to its full size
cells.ask: Before your next talk with someone you've figured out, bring your fixed picture of them all the way to full size, then set it down and start the conversation empty.
cells.core:
Your quick reading of people has run ahead of what is actually there. You have already finished the picture of someone — their pattern, their motive, their next move — and you hold it as settled. That certainty crosses into steering them toward an ending you decided on early, so they meet a conclusion instead of a person, and the connection loses its air.
There is another way to hold it. Carry that finished picture the whole way to its full size, then put it down. You do not have to discard it. Just stop carrying it into the room. Let the first thing they say be the first thing you take in, not another piece of proof. Walk in without the case built, and there is a fresh place for the two of you to go.

cells.tense: You are at a door that has already closed behind you, watching for a clean read of someone instead of letting yourself have one.
cells.ask: Take a relationship that matters and put one small fixed thing in it that keeps going without your watching — a standing time each week, a short shared practice, a promise with a shape.
cells.core:
The clear read of another person is available and you are not spending it. You wait to be sure what someone really means before you move toward them, so you stay on the outside of the connection and watch it from there. The first honest look at what someone is carrying has been within reach for a while and goes unused, because acting on it seems to ask for a guarantee you do not have.
The way through is not to force feeling you do not have. It is to build one small lasting thing where the connection is thin. Pick a single relationship that matters and give it one regular, concrete commitment you can keep — a same-time-each-week call, ten shared minutes, a promise with a shape. That small structure gives your clear read somewhere to land, and the two of you stop circling the door.
cells.sheetLine: Build one small lasting thing where the connection is only watched.

cells.tense: Right now, pen down, you are already taking in what is happening in a room and calling it nothing you did.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: When a shift in someone catches you — a tiredness, a weight under the words — say what you caught right then, and stop there.
cells.core:
You are already taking in what is really happening around you — the shift in someone's face, the thing they are not saying, the current under the words. You do it so fast and so constantly that you would not call it reading. It feels like the room being the room. But you are the one doing it, and the reading is yours.
To claim it, meet what arrives as it arrives, in small pieces, spoken where the other person can hear. Not a full analysis, not a fix — something you have noticed, said while it is still fresh. 'You seem tired.' 'That sounded heavy.' You do not have to be right. You just have to bring the read out of its privacy, where it can be shared instead of carried alone. That is what turns it into connection and gives the clear look back to you.
cells.sheetLine: You are already reading the room. Say what you notice.

attempts.check: The record states the seat is only at its Seed stage (first expression, not yet grown), so my drafts must not imply a mature relational capacity that is already fully available. A reader could reasonably say that in the Too Much cell they are not 'collecting others' conclusions' but are simply excited by their own insight, and that in the Too Little cell they are not 'watching rather than touching' but are just being appropriately cautious. The asks survive being wrong because each one begins with a concrete micro-action the person can try regardless of the diagnosis, and the Too Much ask is a release of an old conclusion, which is useful even if the person is not actually doing it. The sentence that serves me more than them is in the Too Little sheetLine, 'the bell has been rung,' which is a poetic image that could be confusing if the person is not auditory — replacing it with something more tactile and direct.
